title: Rotation Window Safety Net: coordinated endpoint rotation and client compatibility contract
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: This ticket defines the coordinated endpoint rotation pattern (the "Rotation Window") and the minimum compatibility guarantees Redwood will provide when replacing legacy endpoints with the unified inference API. The goal is to allow product teams to retire legacy transports without unexpected client breakages, while bounding the operational burden on platform and SDK teams.
background: Customers and SDKs rely on a mix of legacy streaming and sync endpoints with divergent behaviors (chunked deltas, SSE framing, longpoll semantics). Previous deprecations exposed gaps in client expectations for partial outputs, reconnection, and idempotency. We need a prescriptive rotation contract that sets timelines, telemetry gates, compatibility shim behavior, and developer-facing guidance.
goals: Provide an operationally bounded path to rotate traffic off a legacy endpoint with a 2- to 8-week Rotation Window
Guarantee minimum request/response behavioral compatibility for common client patterns during the window
Define telemetry gates and rollback criteria to protect customer-critical workloads
Minimize long-term maintenance cost by requiring a short, documented compatibility shim with a hard sunset
out_of_scope: Rewriting customer SDKs to use new protocols (we will provide guidance and adapters only)
Changes to model semantics or tokenization behavior
Enterprise dedicated/private deployment specific network routing changes (handled by infra tickets)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Discovery (1 week): inventory callers for targeted endpoint, list high-usage customers and SDK versions
Phase 1 - Shadow & Telemetry (2 weeks): mirror requests from legacy endpoint into unified API in shadow mode, collect success/failure, latency, and output-diff metrics
Phase 2 - Rotation Window (2-4 weeks): start 5%->50%->100% gradual traffic migration by routing policy, enable compatibility shim for remaining legacy clients with strict TTL
Phase 3 - Graceful Shutdown (7 days): cut legacy endpoint to read-only with a header warning and 503-based ramp if gates fail, then disable
Phase 4 - Post-mortem and SDK outreach (1 week): publish findings, update docs, notify customers with migration steps
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry gates defined and implemented: error-rate < 1% over 15m rolling at each step, median p50 latency delta < 2x baseline, output-diff rate < 0.5% against golden prompt set
Compatibility shim implemented with opt-in flag and automatic expiry at end of Rotation Window
SDK/CLI compatibility examples published for Node, Python, and cURL with clear migration snippets
Runtime can rollback routing policy to legacy endpoint within 10 minutes if gates breach
Customer comms template, deprecation timeline, and support runbook are approved by GtM and Support
client_guidance: Dual-connect pattern: open connection to legacy endpoint and start a parallel call to unified API in shadow mode, use unified API result when available
Idempotency: clients should provide a stable request_id for retries; guidance sample included in SDK snippets
Streaming reconnection: treat the unified API stream as authoritative; implement exponential backoff and resume tokens where supported
Fallback: use the compatibility shim only during Rotation Window and implement feature-flagged fallback to prevent long-term dependency
telemetry_gates: Error-rate gate: reject advancement if >1% non-2xx responses in 15-minute window
Regression gate: reject if output-diff >0.5% against curated golden prompts
Latency gate: reject if p95 latency increases by >2x compared to baseline
Customer-severity gate: immediately rollback if top-10 customers by traffic report functional breakage
